items.title: Johnny Lala Interview, 1960-03-15
items.q: The interviewer states 'He's a very good friend of mine' regarding Tony Perrani. The interviewee (Johnny Lala) does not claim a personal relationship with Tony, only responding to the interviewer's mention of him.

ctx.x: I went down to his house in Miami. Tony Perrani and I went over there and we made some little records on him, a little machine, a little recording machine, you know, and he's got a lot of tunes, you know, he was always writing tunes.

He's never... Tony's in New York. Yeah, I know. He was down here playing at the famous door not so long ago, a few years ago, Tony Perrani. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. He played with the Duke's Addiction ladies, man. I understand he's really worth a lot of money. Tony's right. No, sir. Tony is one of the stupidest... Pardon me, microphone. He's a very good friend of mine. Don't misunderstand. Yeah, I know. The guy has made a gigantic fortune, he and Ted Lewis, and they both blew it away on... Tony Perrani doesn't have a…

items.title: Johnny Lala Interview, 1960-03-15
items.q: I had Tony this. I had more trumpet players.

ctx.x: Did you know Mario Filazzo? Yeah. A bass player? Yeah.

Well, he was good. He was good. He was an all-around man. Then you had Luba Prima. I had Luba Prima, Leon Prima. He was a legitimate. I had Luba Prima, Leon Prima, my little cousin Mike Lala. I had Tony this. I had more trumpet players.
Which Mike Lala are you talking about? The one they call Black Mike? Black Mike's my son. White Mike is your son? Yeah. My son, yeah. He plays a lot of trumpet.
